item.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations.
item.abstract: Developing artificial intelligence (AI)-native experimental laboratories for autonomous scientific exploration with minimal human intervention represents a long-standing goal. Although autonomous experimental systems are emerging1-4, especially in chemical and materials science, they remain largely confined to domains with singular objectives, well-defined workflows and simple instrumentation. This limitation may reflect an 'add-on' architecture that uses AI as a task-specific tool rather than providing it with a global understanding of experiments, especially under engineering-oriented circumstances. Here we present AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments. Through the co-design of models, experiments and instruments, AutoDNA realizes the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework. The system autonomously orchestrates over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to execute core nucleic acid operations including synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing, while human intervention is limited to hardware maintenance tasks, such as reagent and labware replenishment. Across four representative applications, AutoDNA matched expert-optimized enzymatic DNA synthesis yields, accelerated concurrent protocol execution by 3.2-fold, completed an end-to-end DNA data storage cycle with exact recovery of the original digital content, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. AutoDNA establishes a blueprint towards science-as-a-service, accelerating biological discovery and advancing various applications in synthetic biology and information storage.

item.title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation.
item.abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.

item.title: ATP-free fatty aldehyde biosynthesis enables an autonomous lux-based bioluminescence system.
item.abstract: Autonomous bioluminescence systems enable continuous light emission in engineered organisms by genetically encoding both luciferase enzymes and their substrate biosynthetic pathways, offering a powerful platform for non-invasive and long-term monitoring of biological processes. However, bioluminescence output is highly sensitive to substrate availability and host metabolic state, often leading to signal instability under energy-limited conditions. Here, we report an alternative luciferin biosynthetic strategy for the bacterial Lux bioluminescence system in which the adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent LuxEC complex is replaced by α-dioxygenase (αDOX), an enzyme that directly converts fatty acids into fatty aldehydes without consuming ATP. Using machine learning-guided directed evolution, we engineered αDOX variants that markedly enhanced bioluminescence intensity when coupled with bacterial luciferase. The resulting ATP-free Lux bioluminescence system enabled single-cell-level bioluminescence imaging and showed a smaller reduction in light emission than the native LuxCDABE system under several antibiotic treatments, although these experiments do not establish ATP availability as the causal mechanism.

item.title: Photobiocatalytic Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Noncanonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical Dyads and Triads.
item.abstract: Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C-C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of noncanonical amino acids bearing either skipped α,γ-stereochemical dyads or contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads. Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase β-subunit, protein engineering generated complementary enzyme variants that selectively construct three of the four possible α,γ-stereoisomers through biocatalyst-controlled reversal of both remote γ-stereochemistry and proximal α-stereochemistry. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C-C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording α,γ-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient β-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived aminoacrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:<0.1:<0.1 d.r. and >99:1 e.r. To further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this platform, the stereochemically enriched amino acids were transformed into valuable γ-chiral amines through engineered PLP-dependent tryptophan decarboxylases, establishing a dual PLP enzyme-based biocatalytic cascade for the enantiodivergent synthesis of privileged amine scaffolds. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme-controlled γ-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates π-π interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.

item.title: Coiled Coils as a Programmable Platform for Computational Biosensor Design.
item.abstract: Coiled coils are a versatile class of α-helical protein motifs characterized by recurring sequence patterns that direct their assembly into defined oligomeric bundles and underpin a wide range of biological functions. The well-established sequence-structure relationships governing coiled-coil formation enable predictive control over stability, specificity, and oligomerization state, making them attractive and chemically tractable building blocks for biosensor design in applications ranging from single-molecule detection to synthetic biochemical circuits and functional nanomaterials. After revisiting the theoretical foundations of coiled-coil architecture, this review outlines strategies to engineer programmable binding interfaces that can be rationally tuned to generate orthogonal, high-affinity interaction pairs, enabling flexible and modular biosensor platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances in computational and data-driven design approaches, including machine-learning and AI-based strategies, alongside established rational and empirical methods for coiled-coil construction. These complementary design principles underpin the development of coiled-coil-based biosensors and are discussed together with selected application examples to illustrate how engineered coiled-coil interactions support sensitive and specific molecular recognition as well as switchable control in synthetic biology and chemical biology. Overall, this review highlights coiled coils as programmable, stable, and highly designable scaffolds at the interface of molecular engineering, computation, and chemical biology.

item.title: Aerobic electrical ATP synthesis at mild redox potentials.
item.abstract: Combining electrochemical and biochemical energy conversion approaches offers exciting opportunities for sustainable biotechnological applications. Here, we present an electrochemical system that directly powers oxidative phosphorylation under aerobic conditions at a mild redox potential of -0.16 V vs Ag/AgCl (0.05 V vs. SHE) by delivering electrons to a minimal respiratory chain reconstituted in liposomes. Using phenazine methosulfate (PMS) or its derivative as redox mediators, electrons are transferred across lipid membranes to cytochrome c, subsequently driving cytochrome aa₃ oxidase activity and ATP synthesis via F1FO ATP synthase. Furthermore, we extend this approach to native sub-mitochondrial particles (SMPs) extracted from bovine heart, demonstrating that such electrochemical reduction can also energise complex, natural respiratory machinery and support ATP production. This work establishes a novel strategy towards coupling electrical inputs to both minimal and native oxidative phosphorylation systems, paving the way for scalable biohybrid energy conversion technologies.

item.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping.
item.abstract: Adapting crops to intensive cultivation systems under climate change requires varieties that combine yield potential with optimized flowering and maturation1,2. In central and eastern China, barley has long been cultivated in a double-season cropping system, in which early flowering and maturation are critical for escaping presummer terminal heat stress and enabling flexible rotation with summer crops3,4. Here we trace the genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China using 505 representative cultivars and identify a flowering-time module defined by a single amino acid substitution in PHYTOCHROME C in combination with a winter-type VERNALIZATION 1 haplotype that underpins this adaptation. The derived allele accelerates heading and maturity, and its frequency has risen sharply in modern autumn-sown varieties. Using base editing in barley and wheat, we confirm causality and demonstrate that this flowering-time combination module, PhyC-VRN1, is functionally conserved across Triticeae. Our results identify and experimentally validate a breeding-relevant flowering-time module that has been selected during modern breeding to enable intensive crop rotations, as well as demonstrate how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct such adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

item.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics.
item.abstract: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. Well-defined internal cavities and engineerable interior and exterior surfaces enable the spatial organization of therapeutic cargoes, molecular recognition elements, and bioactive components within a single nanoscale platform. In this Review, we examine the structural organization, self-assembly mechanisms, physicochemical properties, and functional diversity of representative protein nanocages, including ferritin, the pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 core, DNA-binding proteins from starved cells (Dps), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), encapsulins, and lumazine synthase. We discuss how their structural features and assembly behavior govern biological performance and support biomedical applications in targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and in vivo and in vitro diagnostics. Beyond describing individual platforms, we establish a unifying framework that positions protein nanocages as programmable molecular organizers and highlights five transferable design principles: multivalent ligand display, spatial compartmentalization, receptor-guided targeting, reporter organization and signal enhancement, and stimulus-responsive cargo release and functional activation. We also examine persistent challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation, alongside emerging opportunities in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational protein design. Collectively, these principles establish protein nanocages as versatile biomaterial platforms for integrating sensing, targeting, imaging, and therapy within a single molecular architecture, providing a foundation for next-generation precision nanomedicine. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Reviews typically treat protein nanocages individually, obscuring shared structural features and the extent to which design strategies transfer across systems. This Review addresses this gap by establishing a comparative framework spanning structurally diverse nanocages and distilling their similarities into a concise set of generalizable design principles. It reframes protein nanocages not merely as passive delivery vehicles but as programmable molecular scaffolds that organize cargo with controlled spatial arrangement and stoichiometry. This framework provides biomaterials researchers with a transferable basis for engineering protein assemblies for precision nanomedicine while identifying key challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing that must be addressed to facilitate clinical translation.

item.title: Microbial CO2 bioconversion: integrating carbon fixation pathways and sustainable biomanufacturing.
item.abstract: The continued rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) concentrations has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions while generating value-added products. In this context, microbial CO2 bioconversion has emerged as a promising biological strategy within broader carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) frameworks, particularly through biological carbon capture and utilization (bio-CCU). These approaches enable the conversion of inorganic carbon into fuels, chemicals, biomaterials, proteins, and other value-added products. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent advances in microbial CO2 bioconversion by bridging biological, technological, and industrial perspectives. Unlike previous reviews focusing on individual topics, such as carbon fixation pathways, gas fermentation, or metabolic engineering, this work presents an integrated framework connecting natural and synthetic carbon fixation pathways, microbial production platforms, metabolic engineering strategies, product diversification, and techno-economic considerations. To support this analysis, we conducted a systematic bibliometric assessment of 913 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, revealing sustained growth in scientific output, increasing interdisciplinarity, structured collaboration networks, and strong thematic interconnections across microbial ecology, carbon fixation, metabolism, and carbon utilization. Recent advances in synthetic biology, systems-level metabolic engineering, microbial electrosynthesis, bioelectrochemical systems, synthetic microbial consortia, and artificial intelligence-assisted strain engineering are discussed as important drivers of microbial carbon utilization. The review also critically examines major barriers to industrial implementation, including CO2 mass transfer, carbon fixation efficiency, energy constraints, process scale-up, downstream processing, and economic feasibility. By integrating systematic bibliometric evidence with a critical assessment of microbial CO2 biomanufacturing, this review identifies the convergence of microbial physiology, metabolic engineering, bioprocess development, renewable energy, and data-driven approaches as central to advancing biological CO2 conversion toward scalable, sustainable biomanufacturing.

item.title: Donor-tailored MSC-EVs for osteoarthritis phenotypes: source heterogeneity, engineering, and precision therapy.
item.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a highly heterogeneous degenerative joint disease comprising distinct clinical phenotypes. Recently, mesenchymal stem cells-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) have emerged as a promising cell-free therapeutic approach. While MSC-EVs from diverse sources share fundamental therapeutic mechanisms, they also possess source-specific properties. However, the therapeutic efficacy of EVs is limited in treatments without considering the OA phenotypic diversity. This review aims to elucidate the biological heterogeneity of MSC-EVs derived from diverse tissues (bone marrow, adipose, umbilical cord, and others). By comparing their molecular mechanisms in OA, we outline a potential donor-tailored approach that may inform matching of MSC-EV sources to predominant OA phenotypes. Furthermore, to overcome the limitations of native EVs in targeted delivery and in vivo half-life, we apply frontier bioengineering paradigms, including cellular preconditioning, genetic engineering, cargo loading, and integration with biomaterial scaffolds. Collectively, these advanced methodologies significantly enhance the targeting capability, intra-articular retention, and phenotype-specific therapeutic potency of MSC-EVs. Finally, we delineate current challenges and future research directions, establishing a theoretical foundation to accelerate the clinical translation of donor-tailored MSC-EVs as a precise and effective therapeutic approach for OA.

item.title: Simulation-based Bayesian deep learning enables uncertainty-aware tumor fraction estimation in cell-free DNA.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estimating tumor fraction from whole-genome cell-free DNA sequencing is critical for liquid biopsy, but is hampered by weak signals and baseline noise at low tumor fractions. Existing computational methods often require matched controls or large labeled datasets for training and lack uncertainty quantification. To address these gaps, we developed purNPE, a Bayesian deep-learning framework trained without labeled cancer cell-free DNA samples. Specifically, purNPE leverages a two-part generative model: one component simulates diverse tumor copy-number profiles based on evolutionary genealogies, while a second, data-driven component learns and replicates realistic sequencing background patterns from cancer-free cell-free DNA. By training a Neural Posterior Estimator on synthetic tumor profiles augmented with learned noise, purNPE performs amortized inference in milliseconds without needing a reference sample set at inference.
RESULTS: In a real-world pan-cancer cohort, purNPE achieved comparable performance with existing methods against an orthogonal mutant-allele-fraction proxy (MAE [Formula: see text]). In semi-synthetic and in silico experiments, purNPE showed calibrated uncertainty estimates and a dose-response across low tumor-fraction spike-ins, with separation of approximately 1% TF spike-ins from blanks under the evaluated conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: This work provides a proof-of-concept framework for using simulation-based inference to derive calibrated, uncertainty-aware TF estimates. Larger prospective cohorts with stronger orthogonal ground truth are required before analytical sensitivity or clinical utility can be established.

item.title: An educational activity tailored for undergraduate students on AI-driven nanobody design for targeted antiviral therapeutics.
item.abstract: Protein-based biologics are converging at an unprecedented pace as generative artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes early-stage drug discovery. Nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy chain-only immunoglobulins, are an emerging class of antiviral biologics prized for their small size, stability, and access to cryptic viral epitopes. Traditional nanobody discovery relies on animal immunization and phage display screening, a process that can take 6 to 12 months and is entirely inaccessible within a standard undergraduate laboratory session. Here, we describe a succinct, in silico-based laboratory activity that uses a generative AI protein design server, GeoFlow-V3 (https://prot.design/), to allow undergraduate students to design a novel antiviral nanobody against the influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) protein. This activity builds on our group's prior use of generative AI for undergraduate siRNA design teaching and extends the same pedagogical model to structural protein engineering. To our knowledge, this is the first use of a generative AI protein design platform for teaching nanobody design at the undergraduate level.

item.title: Aldehyde dehydrogenases for oligo-isoprene aldehyde oxidation in Rhodococcus sp. RDE2.
item.abstract: The microbial degradation of natural rubber (NR), which is mainly composed of cis-1,4-polyisoprene, is a promising sustainable strategy for rubber waste treatment. In rubber-degrading actinomycetes, the polymer is cleaved by the latex-clearing protein (Lcp) into oligo-isoprene aldehydes (OIA), which are then oxidized and channeled into the β-oxidation pathway. Some strains employ heterodimeric molybdenum hydroxylases (OxiAB) for this oxidation, whereas others, including Gordonia and Nocardia strains, lack oxiA/oxiB adjacent to lcp and instead use NAD(P)+-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenases (ALDHs); however, the ALDH repertoire differs among strains. Here, we identified the ALDHs responsible for OIA oxidation in Rhodococcus sp. RDE2. Cell-free extracts oxidized OIA preferentially with NAD+, although substantial NADP+-dependent activity (~37% of the NAD+-dependent activity) was also detected. Neither activity was induced during NR growth. Six candidate ALDHs were selected by combining homology searches, qRT-PCR, and heterologous expression analyses in Escherichia coli. Among the purified candidates, only LPH33_RS08240 and LPH33_RS17900 exhibited substantial NAD+-dependent OIA-oxidizing activity, which was 2.0- and 1.3-fold higher than that of the reference VH2 ALDH (GPOL_c02580), respectively. Deletion of either gene reduced both NR and OIA oxidation activities, identifying these two enzymes as major contributors to NAD+-dependent OIA oxidation in RDE2 and, to our knowledge, as the first OIA-oxidizing ALDHs identified in the genus Rhodococcus. Double knockouts did not abolish these activities, indicating contributions from additional ALDHs, consistent with the NADP+-dependent activities detected for the three other candidates. These findings extend the OIA-oxidizing ALDH repertoire of rubber-degrading actinomycetes and provide a foundation for engineering rubber-derived bioconversion. KEY POINTS: LPH33_RS08240 and RS17900 are the first OIA-oxidizing ALDHs found in Rhodococcus. Deleting both genes lowers rubber growth and OIA activity without abolishing either. NADP+-linked ALDHs may couple rubber degradation to reductive biosynthesis in RDE2.

item.title: Circulating cell-free DNA and plasma nuclease activity in human aging.
item.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is an emerging biomarker of aging, but age-related changes in its abundance, oxidation, and plasma nuclease activity have rarely been examined together. We measured plasma cfDNA concentration and nuclease activity in 418 community-dwelling participants aged 7-95 years and quantified 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-oxodG) in cfDNA from 333 participants. cfDNA concentration increased and nuclease activity decreased across ages 7-80 years, whereas participants aged 81-95 years showed lower cfDNA concentration and higher nuclease activity than the 61-80-year group. The cfDNA-to-nuclease activity ratio peaked at 61-80 years and declined thereafter. cfDNA 8-oxodG content increased with age and was highest in the oldest group. The estimated plasma concentration of DNA-bound 8-oxodG rose sharply up to approximately 45 years and then plateaued. An exploratory composite index integrating cfDNA concentration, oxidation, and nuclease activity increased up to approximately 45 years and subsequently stabilized. These cross-sectional findings identify coordinated age-related changes in cfDNA burden, oxidation, and extracellular nuclease activity and support further mechanistic studies of oxidized cfDNA turnover in human aging.

item.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
item.abstract: Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack. […]

cards.score_reason: HBM内存技术关键
cards.title_cn: 全栈协同设计破解 AI 内存瓶颈：NVIDIA 率先采用 HBM4
cards.one_liner: NVIDIA 通过全栈协同设计并率先采用 HBM3e、HBM4，应对 GPU 内存压力。
key_findings: 大模型、长上下文与智能体应用推高 GPU 内存压力，而内存供应趋紧、价格上涨。
NVIDIA 与内存伙伴紧密合作，率先将 HBM3e、HBM4 引入加速计算栈。
全栈协同设计旨在从每字节中挖掘更多性能，缓解内存瓶颈。
cards.why_it_matters: 内存带宽与容量是合成生物学 AI 模型（蛋白设计、基因组语言模型）训练推理的关键瓶颈；HBM4 路线影响算力规划与成本。

item.title: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents
item.abstract: AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task. As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those […]

cards.score_reason: CPU与智能体架构相关

key_findings: AI 智能体在搜索、查库、写测代码等步骤依赖 CPU，并在 GPU 推理与 CPU 执行间切换。
Vera 定位为兼顾最高吞吐与最快智能体响应的 CPU，面向规模化部署智能体的 AI 工厂。
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学智能体常需调度数据库查询、序列设计与代码执行；CPU 吞吐与延迟直接影响自动化实验闭环效率，值得关注其与 GPU 协同架构。
